title: Independent modifiers commute when they target separate fields
summary: GDT575 distinguishes adjacent and interrupted relation/modifier slots. A semantic law can require two modifiers to commute only when they target disjoint fields; a scope-sensitive operator predicts order-dependent output.

design.mechanism: field-disjoint modifier commutation versus ordered semantic scope
design.contrast: Swap two disjoint modifiers in a matched construction: the typed field outputs should remain unchanged under commutation. If one modifier scopes over the other, swapping changes the output or makes the construction invalid.
design.prediction: The old atlas preserved written order and German renderer attachment but did not test a semantic commutation law against an order-sensitive rival.
design.countermodel: A renderer or position-conditioned convention can reproduce the observed layouts without the proposed semantic law.
design.falsifier: A swap changes the typed output despite disjoint fields, or an order-sensitive effect appears only after importing renderer labels.
design.principal_risk: Need independently typed fields and a matched swapped construction; current field labels are not gold.
design.smallest_test: Use two existing adjacent/interrupted pairs and define disjointness from a nonsemantic slot relation before checking outputs.
design.prior_duplicate_pointers: Nearest GDT575/GDT577 and IDEA000018; this proposal is the algebraic commutation falsifier, not order preservation.
design.selection_status: raw unreviewed; no readiness or novelty claim
